newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold end down on professional sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold end down on professional sales.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended slightly down on Thursday from its New York close, pushed down by overseas professional selling prior to the over-the-counter options expiry later this evening, gold traders said.
"We saw some professional selling from Europe," said one source, noting that some speculators were likely liquidating positions prior to the OTC options expiry later on Thursday.
Other sources reported professional selling from Australia following the lower New York close on Wednesday.
"Some Aussie guys were trying to sell after the bad New York close on Wednesday," one gold dealer said.
New York closed at US$382.60/383.10 on Tuesday, and slipped on Wednesday to close at US$382.40/80.
Sources saw strong support for gold at around US$380-381 but said that the metal would remain stuck within a range.
Hong Kong bullion ended at US$382.00/50 an ounce Thursday against New York's US$382.40/80 close.
Local gold ended HK$8 lower at HK$3,521 a tael
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged from its Wednesday fix at -6.
"At -6, the rate is about equal to the Hong Kong dollar interbank rate, meaning that physical demand at the Exchange is not particularly strong," said a senior bullion trader at a local bank.
